snip.t: Immune system (specifically T-lymphocytes): CD4+ T-lymphocytes are central to cell-mediated immunity, particularly against intracellular pathogens and fungi like *Pneumocystis jirovecii*.
The inflammatory component is driven by Th2-type T lymphocytes which facilitate IgE synthesis through production of IL-4 and eosinophilic inflammation through IL-5
● NHL is a diverse group of solid tumors which occurs with the malignant transformation and growth\nof B or T lymphocytes or their precursors in the lymphatic system.
T-lymphocyte defects (congenital or acquired by chemotherapy, AIDS, or malignancy) are associated with an increased risk of Listeria monocytogenes infections of the CNS.
Immune system: Macrophages (phagocytosis, granuloma formation), T-lymphocytes (cell-mediated immunity, cytokine production), granuloma structure (caseous necrosis, fibrous cuff).
The risk of PCP significantly increases as the CD4+ T-lymphocyte count drops.
The CD4+ T-lymphocyte: The central coordinator of adaptive cell-mediated immunity.

qs.q: Which clinical feature is characteristic of T-lymphocyte defects, whether congenital or acquired via chemotherapy, AIDS, or malignancy?
o: High incidence of Streptococcus pneumoniae empyema
Increased risk of Listeria monocytogenes CNS infections
Predilection for Gram-negative enteric shunt abscesses
qs.e: T-lymphocyte defects are associated with an increased risk of Listeria monocytogenes infections of the CNS. Neisseria infections are instead linked to complement and properdin pathway deficiencies.

qs.q: A 19-year-old university student presents with fever, severe pharyngitis, generalized lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly. A peripheral blood smear reveals atypical lymphocytes. What is the primary host cell type destroyed by cytotoxic T-lymphocytes in this condition?
o: Dendritic cells located in lymph nodes
Epithelial cells located in salivary glands
qs.e: Infectious mononucleosis caused by EBV induces a host response where cytotoxic T-lymphocytes appear as atypical lymphocytes to destroy EBV-infected B-cells. Epithelial cells serve as the initial site of viral replication rather than the target of CTL destruction.

qs.q: A 25-year-old man presents with a well-circumscribed, pigmented skin lesion on his trunk that has developed a symmetric, surrounding zone of depigmentation over the past two months. Histologic examination of the depigmented margin reveals a dense dermal infiltrate composed predominantly of CD8+ T lymphocytes surrounding nevus cells. What is the underlying pathophysiologic process of this finding?
o: Complement-mediated microvascular thrombosis in the dermis
Host immune response directed against melanocytes
Malignant clonal proliferation of atypical keratinocytes
Granulomatous destruction of dermal elastic fibers
qs.e: A halo nevus involves a T-cell-mediated immune response targeting shared antigens on both nevus cells and normal epidermal melanocytes. Granulomatous destruction of elastic fibers is characteristic of other dermal elastolytic conditions rather than immune-mediated depigmentation.

qs.q: A virology student analyzes a chronic viral infection where the host liver damage is primarily driven by cytotoxic T lymphocytes attacking infected hepatocytes rather than direct viral cytopathic effects. Which virus typically exhibits this pathogenesis?
qs.e: Hepatitis B liver damage is largely immune-mediated, caused by the host's own cytotoxic T lymphocytes and inflammation rather than direct viral killing. Rhinovirus and rotavirus cause acute lytic infections rather than immune-mediated chronic hepatitis.

qs.q: Which subtype of T lymphocytes directly targets and destroys infected or cancerous cells presenting foreign antigens?
qs.e: Cytotoxic T cells directly target and destroy infected, cancerous, or foreign antigen-presenting cells. Helper T cells assist other cells by releasing cytokines rather than directly killing targets.

qs.q: Which type of immunity is primarily mediated by T lymphocytes targeting intracellular pathogens and tumor cells?
qs.e: T lymphocytes are critical for cell-mediated immunity, whereas B lymphocytes handle humoral immunity via antibodies. Both cooperate within the adaptive immune system.

qs.q: A study of pathologic findings in the islets of Langerhans is performed. It is observed that insulitis may occur in the islets. The inflammatory infiltrate is predominantly composed of T lymphocytes. Which of the following complications is most likely to occur as a consequence of insulitis?
qs.e: An insulitis can precede the development of type I diabetes mellitus. Actually, it is rare to see it because by the time the patients present with overt diabetes mellitus, the islets are long gone. The presence of the T lymphocytes suggests an autoimmune component to the pathogenesis.

qs.q: A cytotoxic T lymphocyte kills a virus-infected cell primarily by:
o: Releasing TNF to activate the mitochondrial pathway
Expressing Fas ligand to engage death receptors
Secreting granzymes that directly activate caspases
Producing reactive oxygen species that damage DNA
qs.e: CTLs express FasL on their surface, which binds Fas on target cells, triggering the extrinsic apoptosis pathway. While CTLs also use perforin/granzymes (c is tempting), the PRIMARY and most efficient mechanism is Fas-FasL interaction. This is why Fas deficiency causes impaired viral clearance.
